new_results.name: QFORM-CAP1-QUADRATIC-RESIDUAL-FLOOR-1OVER180-v1
new_results.statement: For every probability density f<=1 and all real alpha,beta, E(X^2-alpha X-beta)^2>=1/180; sharp for a translated unit interval.

new_results.name: QFORM-SHARP-FROBENIUS-VARIANCE-RIGIDITY-v1
new_results.statement: For independent cap-one inputs with finite fourth moments, Var(X^T A X)>=||A||_F^2/180, with the sharper physical-coordinate bound diag/180 + offdiag/36. Constant 1/180 is sharp.

new_results.name: QFORM-CANONICAL-GAUSSIAN-FOURTH-MODE-GAP-v1
new_results.statement: For the canonical isotropic (1,1,-1) Gaussian core plus an independent fourth square coefficient |lambda|>=delta, the density norm is at most base*[1-eta(1-exp(-delta/4))], eta=P(Z^2>1).

partner_result_applied.application: Extreme-product reduction makes compact finite-fragment indicator laws sufficient for interval concentration; on each such finite-moment witness the new variance theorem yields N_delta(A)<=180 Var(Q)/delta^2.

unresolved_implication: Variance rigidity does not itself bound local density; next attack must couple interval concentration to fixed spectral-tail/high-variance behavior while preserving product provenance.
next_step: Test high-variance locally concentrated compact-fragment witnesses with a fixed spectral floor, or prove a small-ball/variance tradeoff.
